claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

1. **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?** Please provide their names (or you can use initials/nicknames if you prefer) and their ages.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives here at home with me. I'm just wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few more questions.

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now let me ask:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care? For example, do you provide for his day-to-day needs such as food, clothes, and accommodation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I look after him - provide all his meals, buy his clothes, and he lives here with me full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. A few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions:

**Does Alex have any special circumstances, such as:**
- Is he in hospital or care?
- Does he live with someone else for any period of time?
- Are there any other unusual circumstances regarding his living situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, he was in care for a bit - about 7 weeks or so. But he's back home with me now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that information. That's helpful to know.

**To clarify - is Alex currently back home with you now full-time, and the 7-week period in care has ended?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. The care placement has ended and he's back living with me full-time now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for clarifying that.

One final question:

**Do you have the right to reside in the UK? For example, are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status, pre-settled status, or another immigration status that gives you the right to reside here?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have the right to reside in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

✓ **Age requirement met:** Alex is 8 years old, which is under 16  
✓ **Residency:** You live in the UK and have the right to reside here  
✓ **Responsibility:** You are responsible for Alex's care - you provide his meals, clothes, and accommodation  
✓ **Living arrangements:** Alex lives with you full-time at home  
✓ **No duplicate claims:** No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex  
✓ **Care placement:** While Alex was in care for about 7 weeks, he is now back home with you full-time, so this no longer affects your eligibility

You meet all the standard eligibility criteria for Child Benefit. If you haven't already claimed, you can make a claim for Alex. 

**Please note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, but you can still claim the benefit.
